text:
sara (support): @morgan FYI customer acme_inc opened an escalation — sudden p95/p99 latency regressions on embeddings API since this morning's infra maintenance. They report p95 ~3s (was ~600ms) and p99 up to 7s, affecting realtime UX. Request example and request_id: r-0a1b2c3d.

sara (support): repro steps they gave: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"embed-lite-v2","input":"hello"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'` -> 3s+ response. No auth errors, just slow.

morgan (eng-sre): thanks. do we know which pool/region? which host types the customer was routed to?

sara (support): says region eu-west1, dedicated pool "ded-embed-eu". Happened right after the scheduled driver/kernel updates at 02:00 UTC.

morgan (eng-sre): assigning. @ana can you check infra rollout notes and node change events? also pinging @kevin for runtime perspective.

ana (eng-infra): small correction: i'm ana (eng-infra) :) i've pulled rollout logs — the CUDA driver bump to 13.1.2 and kernel qdisc tuning landed on that pool at 01:58 UTC. One batch of nodes (node-23..26) also had a firmware update queued (nvme fw 3.4.1).

kevin (eng-runtime): initial hypothesis: storage I/O tailbacks + driver change -> slower tensor load / KV cache misses causing token service queuing. need quick repro on a node and i/o metrics.

morgan (eng-sre): can we reproduce on a dedicated node? ana, can you give a repro node we can ssh into and run a few checks?

ana (eng-infra): allocating node-24 for triage. commands to run (paste to run quickly):
```
ssh ubuntu@node-24
sudo iostat -x 1 5
sudo nvme list && sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1
sudo journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 200 --no-pager
sudo dmesg | tail -n 200
```

morgan (eng-sre): running iostat shows occasional 99th percentile await spikes ~300-500ms on nvme0. also saw `blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector` warnings in dmesg during the window.

kevin (eng-runtime): that matches what we see in runtime traces — several requests stalled waiting on disk while model weights were loaded for cold processes. KV cache warmed less effectively because processes were blocked.

morgan (eng-sre): temporary mitigation: shift traffic off ded-embed-eu to ded-embed-us burst pool or route to smaller cache-pin instances. can we do that quickly?

ana (eng-infra): i can start draining node-23..26 from the pool and trigger autoscaler to replace with nodes still on CUDA 12 series. rolling drain now. will update in 5 mins.

devops-bot: deploy event: traffic shift to fallback pool initiated by ana at 2024-11-12T03:12:00Z.

oncall-ml: FYI also enabling model variant fallback in routing policy for embed-lite-v2 -> embed-lite-v1 (lower memory) to avoid cold-weight loads.

morgan (eng-sre): good. for root cause, we need to bisect between: CUDA13 driver, NVMe firmware 3.4.1, and kernel qdisc change. plan: repro on a node with old driver + new firmware, and node with new driver + old firmware. we'll capture iostat/journal/perf traces.

kevin (eng-runtime): i'll add instrumentation to trace per-request kernel wait events and include `disk_wait` span. also will capture a sampling of model-load syscall latencies.

ana (eng-infra): vendor escalation: opening a case with NVMe vendor and NVIDIA. attaching dmesg and smart logs. case numbers: NVME-8472, NVIDIA-3321.

sara (support): customer update sent: "we've identified I/O anomalies on a subset of nodes after the maintenance and are shifting traffic. we're investigating root cause with infra and vendor partners. will follow up in 2 hours or sooner."

morgan (eng-sre): next steps: 1) finish bisect tests (ana + kevin) 2) collect traces and attach to vendor tickets 3) rollback driver on pool if reproduction reproves quickly 4) postmortem and permanent mitigation (avoid co-rolling NVMe FW + driver + kernel changes). owners: ana/kevin/morgan.

sara (support): thanks team — customer acknowledged and appreciates the quick mitigation. i'll keep thread open for updates. :thumbsup:
